name: MAKE UP FOR EVER

evidence.summary: MAKE UP FOR EVER's own affiliates page routes sign-up through Rakuten Advertising (create a Rakuten account, request to join the program, then submit the brand's required form; approval can take up to 2 weeks) and publishes the program highlights: '20%+* Commission on all sales' for makeup artists & creators (publishers agree rates directly with the affiliate team at makeupforeveraffiliateteam@assemblyglobal.com), increased rates for high performers, and free samples/product for select creator partners. The page publishes NO statement about an earnings cap or maximum, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for MAKE UP FOR EVER surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

name: amika
description: Salon haircare brand (shampoos, masks, styling and tools sold through salons and Sephora) running a Salon Affiliate Program on Refersion: licensed US cosmetologists get a unique ordering URL for clients and earn 20% commission on sales through it, paid bi-weekly via Trolley once $150 of product has been ordered through the URL in a six-month period.

evidence.summary: amika's own Refersion program page publishes the full Salon Affiliate Program terms: enrollment requires a licensed cosmetologist located in the United States with a current valid license; on acceptance the affiliate receives a unique URL, and once $150 of amika products has been ordered through it within a six-month period, 'a commission in the amount of 20% of the amount of sales made through your URL will be paid to you on a bi-weekly basis' (paid via a Trolley account; commission totals under $30 in any six-month period are not paid out). The terms publish NO statement about an earnings cap or maximum, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed. The page's contact addresses render masked in text form, so no email is recorded.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for amika surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Colorful, shelf-famous haircare with strong routine and transformation content potential for stylist-creators.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A structured salon affiliate program with a client-ordering URL; it is a professional channel rather than an open creator program, and no creator count is published.
reasons.compensation: 20% is a top-tier published rate, but it only starts after $150 of URL sales per six months and no cap statement is published, so the cap stays honestly unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Full terms and application on the brand's Refersion page; the page's email addresses render masked, so no public email is recorded.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Restricted: licensed US cosmetologists only, which excludes general UGC creators.
reasons.credibility: Major professional haircare brand (Amika LLC, Brooklyn NY) sold in salons and Sephora.

evidence.summary: The Allies of Skin North America store's own affiliate page ('Become an ALLIES AFFILIATE') publishes a 'High Commission Rate — From a minimum of 15% and higher depending on performance', exclusive newsletter updates, affiliate-only offers, dedicated affiliate support, bonuses and incentives for top performers, and a 'Special Brand Commission Rates' line ('Earn up to $15k+ per month'). That $15k+ figure is a marketing claim about special rates, NOT a statement that earnings are uncapped, and the page publishes no no-cap/no-maximum statement — so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for Allies of Skin surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: High-potency serums and creams with visible-results positioning are proven premium skincare-UGC material.
reasons.ugc_evidence: An own-store affiliate programme with dedicated support and top-performer bonuses; no hard creator count was published.
reasons.compensation: Minimum 15% rising with performance is a strong published floor, but no cap statement is published, so the cap stays honestly unknown.
reasons.contact_access: Program page on the brand's own North America store; no public affiliate email published on the page.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Programme is presented as open to join from the brand's own page.
reasons.credibility: Internationally distributed premium clinical brand with major beauty-retail presence.

name: Delux Tanners
description: UK sunbed and self-tan brand (tanning creams and intensifiers such as Bubblegum Mania and Tropic Like It's Hot) running an affiliate programme through Shopify Collabs: followers get 10% off with the creator's code, affiliates earn 10% commission on every sale including repeat orders, there is no minimum follower count, and the page states there is no cap on what you can earn, with an invite-only Creator tier above it.

evidence.summary: Delux Tanners' own Collabs page publishes the programme in a stat strip — 10% off for followers, 10% commission on every sale, 0 minimum followers, 'No cap on what you can earn' — and repeats in its programme summary: 'No minimum followers. No earning limits.' Tracking and payment run through the Shopify Collabs dashboard, repeat orders from returning customers count, and regular posters who drive sales can be invited into a higher-rate Creator programme with product to try and payment when content runs as ads. The earnings cap is therefore recorded as uncapped on the brand's own explicit statements.

The page is built around creator content — it lists the content that works (routines, sunbed and holiday glow selfies, unboxings, honest reviews), shows named Delux creators, and offers a paid Creator tier where the brand pays when it runs creator content as an ad.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for Delux Tanners surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Tanning routines and glow results are a defined beauty-UGC niche, though UV-tan positioning narrows the audience versus self-tan-only brands.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A creator-first programme page with content guidance, featured creators and a paid Creator tier on top of the affiliate rate.
reasons.compensation: 10% on every sale including repeats, with the brand's own page stating 'No cap' and 'No earning limits' — verified uncapped at a mid rate.
reasons.contact_access: Short application form on the brand's own Collabs page; applications are reviewed by the brand itself.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to everyone with zero minimum followers — the lowest barrier in this round.
reasons.credibility: Trading UK tanning brand with a live Shopify Collabs programme; smaller and younger than the prestige names in this batch.

name: Luxy Hair
description: Clip-in human hair extensions brand running an Ambassador Program on Aspire: ambassadors share a code/link giving customers $20 off orders of $80+, earn tiered commission of 5% base, 7% after $5,000 in sales and 10% after $10,000, receive free extension sets twice a year, and commit to one original content post per month for a minimum of three months.

evidence.summary: Luxy Hair's own Ambassador Program Terms publish the full structure: the ambassador network is provided by Aspire; 'All ambassadors will earn up to 10% commission' when their code or link is used to redeem $20 USD off orders of $80 USD or more — base 5%, promoted to 7% after $5,000 USD in sales and 10% after $10,000 USD (with demotion after 6 months without converting); customers must purchase within 30 days of click-through; a PayPal address is required at registration; and the brand provides new extension sets twice a year. The terms publish NO statement about an earnings cap or maximum, so commission_cap is recorded as unknown, never guessed. The terms' email addresses render masked in text form, so no email is recorded.

The terms set explicit creator obligations: a minimum 3-month commitment, one piece of unique original content per month (Instagram post/reel/stories, YouTube review or tutorial, or TikTok post) tagging @luxyhair and #luxyhairpartner, following the brand on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, and an exclusivity clause barring promotion of other hair-extension brands while enrolled.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for Luxy Hair surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Extensions are a core hair-UGC category — transformations, tutorials and shade matching are proven formats.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A formal ambassador program with defined monthly content deliverables, tracked tags, and free product sets twice a year.
reasons.compensation: Tiered 5-10% is modest and commission only applies to $80+ orders using the $20-off code; no cap statement is published, so the cap stays honestly unknown. The recorded rate is the published top tier.
reasons.contact_access: Terms and application route on the brand's own site (Aspire network); the terms' email addresses render masked, so no public email is recorded.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Application-based, with a 3-month minimum commitment, monthly posting duty and a no-competing-extensions exclusivity clause.
reasons.credibility: Long-established extensions brand with fully published ambassador terms.

reasons.contact_access: Published support email (info@lyssalashes.com) plus a live GoAffPro signup portal linked from the brand's own article.

With no maximum on what the program pays out, the earnings cap is recorded as uncapped on the brand's own explicit terms. Registrations are reviewed and moderated by the brand.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for FullerSkin surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.ugc_evidence: A complete published affiliate agreement encouraging reviews and blog posts; no creator program extras or hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: Flat 20% on every referred sale with 'no maximum payout' stated twice in the brand's own terms — verified uncapped at a high rate, tempered by the $500 payout threshold and HKD payment.

name: MintPear

evidence.summary: MintPear's own Become A Promoter page publishes the program mechanics: apply with name and email, create your own promo code, and 'For the first month, every time someone uses your code to make a valid, processed, online payment, you'll earn 15% of the sale. There are no limits to how much you can earn, so share away!' — then renew the code each month to continue. The code gives followers free standard shipping on orders $45+ or 10% off the entire store, and payment is via PayPal (PayPal email required) or store credit. The earnings cap is therefore recorded as uncapped on the brand's own explicit statement.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for MintPear surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.ugc_evidence: A promoter model built for social sharing with a personal code and link; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: 15% per code sale with the brand's own page stating 'There are no limits to how much you can earn' — verified uncapped; the monthly code-renewal step adds friction.
reasons.contact_access: Online application form on the brand's own site; no public affiliate email published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application with approval confirmation; promoters must renew their code monthly to keep earning.
reasons.credibility: Small independent cruelty-free brand with a long-running promoter page.

name: BIOS Apothecary
description: All-natural skincare and bath/body brand (BIOS Institute LLC) running its affiliate program on Affiliatly: affiliates earn 10% commission on new-customer purchases made within 30 days of the referral visit (or via their exclusive 10%-off coupon code), track everything in a private portal with creative assets, and are paid in USD via PayPal on the 1st of each month — with the brand's terms stating there is no minimum or maximum payout amount.

evidence.summary: BIOS Apothecary's own Affiliates Program page publishes the offer: 10% commission when a new customer buys via your referral link or 10%-off coupon code, applications reviewed within 24 hours, a private affiliate portal with real-time traffic/sales statistics and creative assets, and payouts 'in US dollars using Paypal on the 1st day of every month. There is no minimum or maximum payout amount.' Signup runs through Affiliatly, linked from the brand's page.

The brand's own Affiliate Terms and Conditions repeat the economics in full: 10% commission on all sales generated within the first 30 days of the referral visit (each order in that window earns), the coupon 'can be used by an unlimited number of customers and never expires', all products eligible, no application fees or minimum sales quotas, and in the Commissions section: 'There is no minimum or maximum payout amount.' With the program's own terms setting no maximum on payouts, the earnings cap is recorded as uncapped.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for BIOS Apothecary surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.

reasons.niche_fit: Natural skincare and bath/body products aimed at beauty editors and bloggers fit clean-beauty content, in a crowded botanical field.
reasons.ugc_evidence: A structured program recruiting editors, bloggers and websites with a creative-assets library; no hard creator count published.
reasons.compensation: 10% is a standard rate, and the brand's own terms state 'no minimum or maximum payout amount' — verified uncapped on payouts.
reasons.contact_access: Signup via the brand's own affiliate page (Affiliatly portal); no public affiliate email published.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Free to join with applications reviewed within 24 hours and no sales quotas.
reasons.credibility: Small natural brand (BIOS Institute LLC) with fully published affiliate terms.

No prerequisites beyond an application form and approval. The cap is recorded as uncapped on the brand's own explicit statement, but the announcement dates from December 2020, so this evidence is marked needs_review.

The brand's published contact on the same page is info@clearskinsolutions.com (808 16th Ave NW, Ardmore, OK). Treat enrollment as unconfirmed until the brand responds.
No Beacons brand page or other hard creator count for Clear Skin Solutions surfaced in this research, so creator saturation is recorded as unknown rather than estimated.
